source_text: Verum pergamus ad reliqua. Nihil prorsus valet, quod te ais diabolo reputare, non corpora, sed delicta; inficiaris omnino, sicut frequenter ostendimus, nullo alio studio, nisi ut Manichaei vites invidiam, cuius inspiras venenum. Corpora enim, prorsus corpora reputas principi tenebrarum, quorum commixtionem diabolicam profiteris, quorum genitalia, quorum motus, quorum fructus accusas. Arguis palam ex primo magisterio membra, non vitia; illud enim dicis diabolicum, quod etiam Manichaeus, sicut in scripturis eius docui, in sexibus indignatur vigere. Et ut repetitione brevi lector noster, quod tenere possit, accipiat; aut ostende esse in parvulis voluntatem, aut ab eis crimen amoveto. Quod cum non facis, sed asseris eos propter hoc a diabolo possideri, quia de corporum sunt commixtione generati; ostendis te non peccata, quae sine voluntate non sunt, sed ipsa corpora adversariae potestati deputare. Ut ergo ea libido, quae et in hominibus et in pecoribus invenitur, naturalis et a Deo instituta est; ita ista libido, quam in disputationis tuae varietate perpeteris, per quam inter varia dogmata contrariaque versaris, non minus a stultitia quam a profanitate concepta est. Haud iniuria ergo Ambrosium a vestra cohorte distinguimus; nec illum, sicut petis, Manichaeum vocamus.
pass_a_gloss: But let us proceed to the rest. Nothing at all avails, that you say you credit to the devil not bodies but offenses; you disown altogether, as we have frequently shown, by no other zeal except that you may avoid the spite of Manichaeus, whose poison you breathe. For bodies, bodies indeed you credit to the prince of darkness, whose mingling you profess diabolical, whose genitals, whose motions, whose fruits you accuse. You openly accuse from the first teaching the members, not the vices; for you say that is diabolical which even Manichaeus, as I taught in his writings, is indignant thrives in the sexes. And that by a brief repetition our reader may receive what he can hold; either show that there is will in little ones, or remove the charge from them. Which since you do not do, but assert that they are possessed by the devil on account of this, because they were generated from the mingling of bodies; you show that you assign not sins, which are not without will, but the bodies themselves to an adversary power. Therefore as that lust which is found both in humans and in cattle is natural and instituted by God; so that lust which you suffer in the variety of your disputation, through which you turn among various and contrary dogmas, was conceived no less from stupidity than from profanity. Not unjustly therefore we distinguish Ambrose from your cohort; nor do we call him, as you ask, a Manichaean.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Let us proceed to the rest. Your claim that you assign offenses to the devil, not bodies, has absolutely no force. As I have frequently shown, you are simply denying the facts, with no aim except to avoid the odium of Manichaeus while breathing his poison. Bodies—quite plainly, bodies—are what you assign to the ruler of darkness: you profess their union devilish and accuse their reproductive organs, their movements, and their offspring. Following your earliest instruction, you openly accuse members, not vices. You call devilish the very thing that Manichaeus too resents seeing flourish in the sexes, as I showed from his writings.

To give the reader in brief repetition something he can retain: either show that infants possess will or remove the charge from them. When you fail to do this and instead assert that the devil possesses them because they were generated from bodily union, you show that you assign to the hostile power not sins, which do not exist without will, but bodies themselves. So the lust found in both human beings and animals is natural and instituted by God. But this lust you suffer in the inconsistency of your argument, through which you move among various and opposing doctrines, is conceived no less from stupidity than from impiety. I therefore rightly distinguish Ambrose from your company and do not call him a Manichaean, as you request.

choices.why: Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
